newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Oct 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Oct 23.

text.p: General Motors Corp and the Canadian Automobile Workers union agreed to settle a strike with a new three-year labor contract, the Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday.
- NYNEX Corp will merge its British-based cable company with units of Cable & Wireless Communications and Bell Canada International.
- Procter & Gamble Co is pulling Luvs diapers out of Europe.
- Nine big public pension funds are unveiling a study that questions the fees charged by leveraged buyout firms.
- Medicare beneficiaries in HMOs are being shortchanged on their rights to appeal certain grievances, a federal judge said.
- Japanese authorities arrested a former copper trader for Sumitomo who is in the center of a $2.6 billion debacle.
- South America's Mercosur trade block has created economic growth by erecting trade barriers, a World Bank study said.
- Digital Equipment Corp reported a quarterly loss following a 16-percent drop in product sales.
- American Home Products Corp, Bristol-Myers Squibb Co and other drug companies reported good earnings for the quarter.
- Salomon Inc reported a 58-percent downturn in quarterly profit.
- Kimberly-Clark Corp's quarterly operating profit beat market expectations.
- Times Mirror Co, Knight-Ridder Inc and Washington Post Co reported better quarterly earnings.
- Medaphis Corp reported a bigger quarterly loss.
- The NASDAQ Composite index fell 16.41 points to 1,220, while the Dow Jones industrial average lost 29.07 at 6,061.80. Bond prices also fell.
- Miami's hiring of investment banker Richard Montalbano to help it resolve its budget crisis has raised some concern among the city's municipal bond community.
